awarding_body.detail: Every page read sits on embo.org, the European Molecular Biology Organization's own domain, inside Funding > Fellowships, grants and career support. The scheme is EMBO's own, named after its donor, and is selected by EMBO's Science Journalism Advisory Board. Not an aggregator, news article, blog, or mirror.
awarding_body.quote: Fellowships, grants and career support - Maria Leptin | EMBO Science Journalism Fellowships - EMBO ... This scheme was made possible by a private donation from Professor Maria Leptin. ... All completed applications will be acknowledged by email.

deadline.detail: The deadline is 30 October each year at 23:59 Central European Summer Time, with a single annual selection round and applications accepted at any time before then. This matches the record's deadline_label word for word and its deadline_date of 2026-10-30. As of today (12 October 2026) the 30 October 2026 deadline is still ahead, so the cycle is currently open; outcomes are notified by mid-November.
deadline.quote: Apply by 30 October ... Fully completed applications must be registered in the EMBO application portal by 23:59 Central European Summer Time on 30 October of each year. Applicants will be notified by email of the outcome of the selection process by mid-November. ... The selection of Fellows and the awarding of fellowships takes place once a year although applications can be submitted at any time.

eligibility.detail: Each distinct claim in the record's eligibility_summary is confirmed verbatim: the employed-or-freelance journalist track requires demonstrable relevant experience as their main occupation and samples of published or broadcast work, with a genuine desire to broaden and deepen their science knowledge; the life-scientist track requires a master's degree or higher and evidence of prior reporting on the life sciences, with a genuine desire to transition into journalism as a profession. Personal blog posts, social media, and academic commentary/review publications are explicitly not accepted as evidence. One material requirement in the record's summary is MISSING rather than contradicted: applicants must reside in an EMBC Member State and their placement/s must also occur in an EMBC Member State (32 states listed on embo.org/about-embo/embc, including Israel and Turkiye). Placements must be in person; virtual placements are not eligible. Applicants are not subject to any age restriction.
eligibility.quote: Applicants must reside in an EMBC Member State, and their placement/s must also occur in an EMBC Member State. The placements must be in-person to maximize opportunities for learning and engagement. Virtual placements are not eligible. ... Applicants are not subject to any age restriction. ... Journalists must be able to demonstrate relevant experience of working as an employed or freelance journalist as their main occupation and provide appropriate samples of their published or broadcast work. ... Life scientists seeking support to transition into full time (science) journalism must have a master's degree or higher, and preferably in a life sciences discipline. ... Personal blog posts or social media postings, or publication in academic journals of commentary or reviews of research, are not considered sufficient evidence of prior journalism.

funding.detail: The award is a stipend, matching the record's funding_type. It is a daily stipend scaled to the cost of living in the placement country and is intended to cover living expenses and travel costs; it is not a tuition award and no tuition or fee waiver is mentioned anywhere on the pages. Fellows pay their own social security contributions, taxes and other costs. Journalist Fellows additionally get travel and accommodation for a two-day workshop at EMBO in Heidelberg. Duration: journalists 3-6 months, researchers transitioning into journalism 3-12 months (longer than 3 months is subject to an ongoing assessment). The exact daily rate is not stated on the pages; it is delegated to the linked subsistence-rates PDF, which I could not read.
funding.quote: Successful applicants receive a daily stipend based on the cost of living in the country of their placement/s. The stipends are intended to cover living expenses and travel costs. Fellows are responsible for their own social security contributions, taxes or other costs incurred. ... For journalists, the duration of the fellowship is for a minimum of three months and a maximum of six months. ... For researchers wishing to become science journalists the duration of the fellowship is for a minimum of three months and a maximum of 12 months.

degree_levels.detail: The record claims degree levels 'Postgraduate, Professional', but none of the pages I read states any degree level the programme offers or awards. The scheme is a funded placement/sabbatical fellowship (a research institution for journalists, a media newsroom for researchers), not a degree programme, so it offers no levels at all. The only degree statement on the page is an entry requirement for one of the two tracks: master's degree or higher for life scientists transitioning into journalism, and 'preferably in a life sciences discipline'. The journalist track has no stated degree requirement. I therefore cannot confirm the record's degree_levels field as the levels the programme actually offers.
degree_levels.quote: Life scientists seeking support to transition into full time (science) journalism must have a master's degree or higher, and preferably in a life sciences discipline.

recommended_field_updates.verification_notes: Re-checked 2026-10-12 against embo.org; the recorded official_source_url resolves and served the full programme, so only the trailing-slash canonical form used by EMBO's own navigation is recommended. Awarding body, deadline (30 October, 23:59 CEST, annual, applications accepted at any time before then) and the stipend funding claim all confirmed verbatim from the official pages; the 2026 cycle is open as of 12 October 2026 with results by mid-November. Two open items: (1) the record's degree_levels 'Postgraduate, Professional' is not supported by any statement on the page - this is a placement fellowship that awards no degree, with only a 'master's degree or higher' entry requirement on the researcher track and no degree requirement on the journalist track, so a human should decide whether to relabel the field; (2) the eligibility_summary omits the EMBC Member State residence-and-placement restriction, which is the single most screening-relevant rule on the page (32 EMBC Member States, in-person placements only, virtual placements ineligible, no age limit) - a candidate reading only the card could wrongly conclude they may apply from anywhere. The exact daily stipend amount is not published on the HTML pages; it is delegated to https://www.embo.org/documents/SEG/SEG_subsistence_rates_and_travel_allowance.pdf, which returned compressed binary and could not be read, so the stipend value is unverified. Next re-check should re-read the Application tab (deadline wording is stable but should be confirmed annually around September) and open the subsistence-rates PDF in a reader.

notes_for_reviewer: Two decisions need a human. First, degree_levels: the record says 'Postgraduate, Professional' but EMBO's pages never state a level offered - this fellowship grants no degree. The only degree text is the researcher-track entry requirement ('must have a master's degree or higher, and preferably in a life sciences discipline'), while the journalist track has no degree requirement. Someone should decide whether degree_levels should be set to something like 'Not a degree programme - placement/sabbatical fellowship' or left as an entry-requirement description; I did not invent a level, so I marked it unconfirmed and kept the verdict off 'active'. Second, eligibility: every claim the record makes is confirmed, but the record's summary omits that applicants must reside in an EMBC Member State and the placement must also be in an EMBC Member State, that placements must be in person (virtual placements are ineligible), that if a Fellow takes two placements at least one must be in a different Member State, that applicants are not subject to any age restriction, that Fellows may not undertake other work during the fellowship, and that journalists must not report on their host research institution. The country field 'Multiple' is technically true (32 EMBC Member States) but reads as worldwide; a human may prefer 'Europe / EMBC Member States'. I did not submit anything to applications.embo.org, so no confirmation number or outcome exists for this record - nothing was fabricated.
